final_candidates.decision_summary: Verified V at position 38. Strong fixed-backbone incompatibility and evolutionary intolerance support destabilization by introducing an acidic residue, although neither establishes unfolding.

Verified W at position 17. Replacing tryptophan with proline could disrupt packing and backbone geometry; structural incompatibility and evolutionary intolerance support this hypothesis without proving it.

Verified F at position 40. Strong fixed-backbone incompatibility supports disruption from replacing an aromatic residue with an acidic residue, while evolutionary evidence is less decisive than for the leading candidates.

stop_reason.detail: Remaining evidence sources are unlikely to change the ranking and cannot directly establish folding disruption or photosystem-I knockout.

history.rationale: Replacing a bulky aromatic residue with an acidic side chain could strongly disrupt hydrophobic packing if W17 is buried. This is a sequence-based destabilization hypothesis, not a measured folding effect.
Retain as an alternative because Asp is absent in homologs and its structural delta is negative. Demote relative to W17P because the structural penalty is substantially weaker.
Low sequence plausibility supports intolerance but does not overcome its weaker prior structural evidence relative to the leading candidates.
Proline removes the tryptophan aromatic packing group and restricts backbone geometry. It could also disrupt backbone hydrogen bonding if this position lies in regular secondary structure.

Retain near the top because structural incompatibility and absence of homologous Pro support disruption. Loss of the aromatic side chain and proline backbone constraints are plausible mechanisms, not proof of unfolding.

Low plausibility supports the existing hypothesis that replacing tryptophan with proline disrupts packing or backbone geometry. The new evidence does not distinguish it from the other zero-scoring candidates.
Introducing an acidic residue into the hydrophobic segment surrounding Y34 could undermine packing and folding stability. The expected severity depends on side-chain burial.

Demote because the positive structural delta fails to support the initial folding-disruption hypothesis. Absence of Asp in homologs keeps it plausible as a deleterious substitution, but does not distinguish folding from functional effects.

Sequence intolerance supports a deleterious effect, but the previous relatively favorable fixed-backbone compatibility limits the unfolding hypothesis. Retain below candidates with stronger structural incompatibility.

Proline at I33 could disrupt an extended structural element through altered backbone geometry and loss of a backbone hydrogen-bond donor. Its placement near native P35 may further perturb local conformation.

Demote to last because Pro is favored by the fixed-backbone model and occurs in approximately 17% of covered homologs. These observations undermine a generic proline-disruption argument at this position.

The likelihood ratio remains below neutral, providing weak support for intolerance rather than evidence of neutrality. Its comparatively greater sequence plausibility and prior structural compatibility leave it last.

Replacing valine with aspartate in this hydrophobic sequence region could introduce an unfavorable charge into a packing interface. Structural evidence is needed to distinguish core destabilization from a surface effect.

Promote to first: the strongest negative backbone-conditioned log-probability delta coincides with no observed Asp in the covered homologs. Replacing a hydrophobic residue with a charged residue provides a plausible disruption mechanism, although burial is not established by these outputs.

Very low sequence plausibility supports intolerance and is consistent with the prior structural ranking. Retain first place without increasing confidence because sequence intolerance does not establish unfolding.
Loss of an aromatic side chain and introduction of an acidic group could disrupt stabilizing hydrophobic contacts. Confidence is limited by unknown burial and local interactions.

Promote provisionally into third on strong incompatibility with this backbone. Asp occurs in approximately 19% of covered homologs, so the confidence is tempered by possible context-dependent tolerance.

Sequence intolerance is consistent with the existing structural concern about replacing an aromatic residue with an acidic residue. Retain third place because no direct folding measurement resolves its comparison with W17P.
This aromatic-to-acidic substitution could destabilize the fold if F48 anchors packing near the glycine-rich region. A solvent-exposed location would weaken that prediction.
Demote because the structural penalty is small and evolutionary coverage is only 20 of 43 homologs. Neither result strongly supports fold disruption.
Low sequence plausibility modestly supports intolerance. Prior structural compatibility and limited local MSA applicability still prevent promotion.

Replacing glycine with a bulkier, beta-branched residue could prevent a tight turn or another glycine-dependent backbone conformation. This candidate is strongly contingent on the experimental backbone geometry.
Moderate structural incompatibility supports retaining this candidate. Val appears in approximately 17% of covered homologs, weakening a general claim that this glycine is indispensable for folding.
The low likelihood ratio provides modest support for intolerance of added side-chain bulk at this glycine. It does not directly demonstrate disruption of a required turn or folding.
